Here's your space and defense news for Tuesday, Nov 3.

Top stories: Russia's widening strikes in the Black Sea near Romania and Bulgaria are testing how far NATO will let things go. The US approved a $2.1B sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, paid for by allies, though deliveries may not come until the 2030s. A coalition led by the UK and France will rehearse a postwar force for Ukraine in Poland from Nov 9 to 22.

NATO

  • Cargo ships near Romania and Bulgaria were hit seven times in October, and NATO is now sending patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the Black Sea. Analysts call it a deliberate Russian test of the alliance's limits. CNA/Reuters
  • Allies worry that if Republicans lose today's midterms, Trump could pull more troops from Europe or cut NATO funding. A review of US forces abroad is due by December. Politico Europe
  • Nordic allies say it's hard to push back on Russian sabotage, escorts for its shadow fleet of tankers, and airspace violations in the Baltic without escalating. Defense News
  • NATO's innovation command, Allied Command Transformation, finished two weeks of experiments in Latvia. It tested communications that keep working under attack, layered counter-drone defense and next-generation targeting. NATO ACT

European Union & European defense

  • The Commission reopened €21.3B in unspent SAFE defense loans. Countries' plans are due by Nov 13, and it's urging them to buy jointly with Ukraine. Eunews
  • Ukraine plans to move up to €1B of its EU loan into the Ukraine Support Instrument, more than four times what's in it now. The money would fund joint production of air defense, drones and ammunition. Euronews
  • EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called for closer EU-UK defense ties ahead of the Nov 20 summit. The UK is still deciding whether to join SAFE's second round. Agence Europe
  • About 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will hold Exercise Koalicja in southeast Poland. It's the first drill for the Multinational Force – Ukraine, the planned postwar force, and it isn't run by NATO. Euronews
  • Germany is weighing a role in GCAP, the fighter program run by the UK, Italy and Japan, after the French-German-Spanish FCAS fighter fell apart. Airbus is getting ready for talks with BAE. The Defense Post
  • At the Euronaval show, France started a partnership with industry to field naval drones faster. It ordered Exail mine-clearing robots and a second large uncrewed combat submarine from Naval Group, and signed a deal with Naval Group and MBDA to double the Aster missile launch cells on its FDI frigates. Defense News
  • From April 2027, foreign suppliers that win UK defense deals worth £50M or more will have to give something back to the UK economy, such as local jobs or investment. The Defense Post

United States

  • The State Department approved a proposed $2.1B sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE Patriot interceptors to Ukraine. Canada, Germany, Norway and the EU's Ukraine loan are paying, and Lockheed is the prime contractor. Breaking Defense
  • Deliveries may not start until the early 2030s, so Kyiv is asking the Pentagon to hand over missiles it already has and replace them later. Military Times
  • The Space Force set up SPACEFOR-SOC at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa. It's the first new service command under US Special Operations Command since 2006. DVIDS
  • The Space Force is looking at launching up to five satellites into the space between Earth and the Moon by late 2029, as a first step toward a larger constellation there. Air & Space Forces Magazine
  • Industry executives say the Space Force's effort to build surveillance satellites on commercial designs is buying too few of them and moving too slowly. SpaceNews
  • SpaceNews says 2028 is the year military space programs have to prove themselves. Demonstrations are due for Golden Dome's space-based interceptors, tracking moving targets from space and refueling satellites in orbit. SpaceNews
  • Lockheed got a $95M change to its GPS IIIF satellite contract, which brings the production contract to $4.73B. SatNews
  • Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll joined OpenAI as a senior counselor on national security. Breaking Defense

European space

  • Ireland, which holds the EU Council presidency, put forward a new compromise draft of the EU Space Act. EU countries still haven't agreed a negotiating position, and the US Commerce and State Departments are reviewing the draft. The European Post
  • Hydrosat announced Nyktos, a high-resolution thermal imaging program for European and NATO defense customers, built at a new facility in Europe. SpaceNews
  • The next Ariane 6 launch, VA271, is set for no earlier than Nov 23. It will carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites and use the four-booster version, the rocket's most powerful. ESA

Global space & defense

  • The hardware for the first flight test of China's crewed Moon program, the Long March 10 rocket and the Mengzhou spacecraft, appears to have arrived at the Wenchang launch site. SpaceNews
  • In a battlefield test, Vantor got satellite images to Ukrainian troops within seven minutes of a request. SpaceNews
  • Rocket Lab's 99th Electron launch carried a radar-imaging satellite for the Japanese company iQPS. SpaceNews
